subject: Data residency & encryption options for Cardinal Health pilot — DPA scoping
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@cardinalhealth.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cardinalhealth.com, legal@cardinalhealth.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood pilot — security questionnaire and residency question

Hi Markus / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited about the latency profile and the model routing options. Our legal and security teams have a couple of follow-ups while we scope the pilot:

- Can Redwood support per-endpoint data residency for the pilot (US-only)?
- For PHI that might be uploaded during testing, do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) or an HSM-backed KMS integration?
- Attached is our short HIPAA intake (Cardinal_HIPAA_Questionnaire.pdf). Please flag items that would be blockers for a scoped 3-month pilot.

Also looping procurement and legal for visibility — we may need a DPA addendum / BAA depending on answers.

Appreciate a short summary (1–2 bullets) we can share internally by EOD Friday.

Best,
Maria Lopez
Program Manager, Cardinal Health

(ps — attaching the questionnaire)

From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, procurement@cardinalhealth.com, legal@cardinalhealth.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot — security questionnaire and residency question

Hi Maria — thanks for the questionnaire and for surfacing the residency question. Quick summary up front:

1) Residency: We can host the pilot in US-only regions. For the hosted Redwood API we support region pinning at the project/route level, and we can provide a scoped residency attestation for pilot data.

2) Keys/encryption: We support two production options: Redwood-managed KMS (default) and customer-managed keys via a KMS/HSM integration (BYOK). For a pilot we can temporarily provide per-tenant envelope encryption with Redwood-managed KMS and prep a BYOK path if you need it for production.

3) DPA/BAA: We have a BAA template (happy to share a redline). For pilot scoring, Legal often signs our scoped pilot addendum that references the BAA and limits data categories during the test window.

I've attached: Redwood_DPA_Draft_v1_redline.docx (initial DPA + pilot addendum) and Redwood_KMS_Attestation.pdf (high-level KMS/HSM controls).

Next steps I suggest:
- Monica and I to provide a 1‑page pilot security summary for your security review (target Thu EOD).
- If legal wants BYOK for the pilot, we can run a short feasibility checklist and timetable — BYOK for a hosted pilot typically takes 3–4 weeks.
- Procurement: if Cardinal is fine with the scoped pilot addendum, we can issue a trial SOW.

Will follow up with the 1‑pager.

— Markus Klein
GM, Enterprise Sales (Regulated Verticals)
Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@cardinalhealth.com>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, legal@cardinalhealth.com
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot — security questionnaire and residency question

Thanks Markus — attaching the 1‑page summary for security: scope, controls, and recommended guardrails.

Key clarifications included in the summary:
- Data flows: ingest -> model -> ephemeral KV caches -> outputs. We recommend disabling telemetry for the pilot and restricting uploaded assets to test PHI tokenized variants.
- KV caching: cache eviction policy can be set to immediate expiry for pilot routes to avoid persistent context storage.
- Auditing: we can enable request-level logs for the pilot and provide a time-bound export.

On BYOK: if Cardinal prefers BYOK during the pilot we will need a short intake with your security/ops team to exchange key policies and validate allowed operations (encrypt/decrypt/rotate). That intake typically includes: key material format, rotation window, and principle mapping.

Maria — can you confirm whether your security team would accept a scoped BYOK intake in our pilot window or whether BYOK is an absolute must before any test PHI is uploaded?

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: CH-Pilot-Security-Summary.pdf)

From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@cardinalhealth.com>
To: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cardinalhealth.com, legal@cardinalhealth.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot — security questionnaire and residency question

Monica / Markus — thanks for the fast turnaround and the summary. Quick internal note: Legal flagged that for some pilot datasets they want BYOK or at least proof that keys are tenant-isolated and that Redwood's staff cannot access plaintext. Security would accept a scoped BYOK intake but their preference is: if BYOK is not feasible within pilot timeframe, we need a written operational control that keys are tenant-scoped, with an attestation and a plan for production BYOK.

Procurement is also asking about cost impact for BYOK vs Redwood-managed KMS and whether the pilot SOW can include a statement of work to enable BYOK if the pilot goes to production.

Can you provide:
- Short attestation language saying Redwood supports tenant-scoped envelope keys and that Redwood staff do not have direct access to customer KEKs (we can use the provided KMS attestation for this).
- High-level BYOK enablement timeline and cost delta for Dedicated vs Hosted pilot.

If you can send those two items Monday morning, we can push an internal approval for the pilot.

Thanks,
Maria
(on behalf of Cardinal Legal & Security)

From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, procurement@cardinalhealth.com, legal@cardinalhealth.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot — security questionnaire and residency question

Maria — appreciate the clarity. Below are the two requested items (summary / attestation + BYOK timeline + cost notes). I will also drop these into the Drive link and the Docusign envelope for the pilot addendum.

1) Attestation language (suggested):
"Redwood Inference attests that during the scoped pilot, customer data pinned to a US-only project will be stored in US regions. Envelope keys used for at-rest encryption can be tenant-scoped such that Redwood personnel cannot derive customer KEKs. Redwood maintains administrative controls over the platform but does not possess the plaintext customer key material when BYOK is enabled. For Redwood-managed KMS, Redwood personnel have the same operational access as described in the attached Redwood_KMS_Attestation.pdf."

2) BYOK enablement — high level:
- Hosted pilot: BYOK feasibility assessment + key exchange process — 2–3 weeks (security intake + policy validation). BYOK production rollout typically 4–6 weeks after pilot sign-off.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): can shorten BYOK enablement to 2–3 weeks in many cases due to private infrastructure and coordination with our cloud partner; there is an ops onboarding fee for Dedicated environments.

3) Cost notes (high level):
- BYOK itself does not incur a licensing surcharge; costs come from operational onboarding and any Dedicated environment fees. Estimated one-time onboarding: $8k–$20k depending on integration complexity (HSM vs cloud-KMS tie-ins).
- Dedicated capacity/throughput is contracted separately; we can provide an SOW for the initial 3-month pilot.

Next steps:
- Monica and I will update the DPA redline with the attestation sentence and re-attach the scoping SOW.
- If Cardinal confirms BYOK is desired for pilot, please share the security contact for the intake (email + POC).

I'll follow up Monday with updated DPA and SOW docs in the Drive link.

Cheers,
Markus

On behalf of Redwood Inference
